Status

FinKore Core 2.0.4 stable.

Purpose

This document defines a need for an Approval Decision from an eligible Actor or application-defined subject. Eligibility may refer to an individual Actor, role, group, organizational responsibility, or another declared rule; no authorization or RBAC model is prescribed.

Requirements

  • APPROVAL-REQUIREMENT-001 — An Approval Requirement MUST have a stable identifier within its approval context.
  • APPROVAL-REQUIREMENT-002 — It MUST identify the subject whose approval is requested.
  • APPROVAL-REQUIREMENT-003 — It MUST identify its eligible Actor, application-defined subject, or eligibility rule.
  • APPROVAL-REQUIREMENT-004 — It MUST define which Approval Decision outcome satisfies or rejects it.
  • APPROVAL-REQUIREMENT-005 — An applicable Approval Requirement with no effective Approval Decision MUST have the PENDING State.
    Evidence & context1 research note+

    These sources inform discussion of this rule. Their role and limits are stated separately; a citation is not certification or specialist sign-off. Passages from the same study or consultation are not independent confirmation.

    Research / Illustrates a risk

    Monitoring evidence is not an eligible business approval ↗

    Francesca Nyarkoa Kobla; Jessica Fosua Agyei

    Pending status and eligible business decision-makers cannot be replaced by monitoring output or technical access. Organizational monitoring and segregation-of-duties policy remain separate.

    Scope and limitations

    A product can combine these controls in one interface, but their evidentiary questions differ. The review is a synthesis, not a causal test of any particular approval implementation.

  • APPROVAL-REQUIREMENT-006 — Eligibility MUST be evaluated independently from the Actor's technical ability to submit a request.

    Research / Supports the rationale

    Changing the representation does not establish equivalent control ↗

    Mysore Ramaswamy; Richard Calvasina; Eugene Calvasina; Gerald Calvasina

    Changing document representation does not itself satisfy the applicable declared financial predicates or eligibility. The historical voucher example motivates control preservation without mandating procurement rules or a document package.

    Scope and limitations

    The transfer to FinKore is reviewer inference. The article’s legal assertions, Just-In-Time process and document package are not verified as current or universal. A syntactically valid message does not itself establish payment eligibility.

  • APPROVAL-REQUIREMENT-007 — A requirement MAY be conditional as defined by Conditions.
  • APPROVAL-REQUIREMENT-008 — After all required Decision structure, scoped association, eligibility, lifecycle, relevant-fact or revision, expiration, and explicit-context validation succeeds, an applicable standalone Approval Requirement MUST derive its State from the complete effective Decision set: one or more effective REJECTED Decisions MUST yield REJECTED; otherwise one or more effective APPROVED Decisions MUST yield APPROVED; otherwise the Requirement MUST yield PENDING. Decision order, Actor equality, decision-timestamp order, and repeated matching outcomes MUST NOT change this aggregation. A later timestamp MUST NOT imply withdrawal or supersession.

    These sources inform discussion of this rule. Their role and limits are stated separately; a citation is not certification or specialist sign-off. Passages from the same study or consultation are not independent confirmation.

    Research / Illustrates a risk

    Timestamp precedence cannot replace the defined aggregation of effective approvals ↗

    Abhilash Katari

    When opposing decisions remain valid and effective, defined aggregation and preserved history govern the result. A later timestamp alone is neither withdrawal nor supersession; LWW is not universally prohibited.

    Scope and limitations

    The example assumes both opposing Decisions are valid and still effective. Legitimate withdrawal/supersession differs from timestamp overwrite. LWW may still suit a cache or application value whose declared semantics permit it.

Invariants

An Approval Requirement must not be considered approved without an effective approving Approval Decision from an eligible Actor.

Concrete record and Requirement/Decision evaluation boundaries require the subject and eligibility declarations in APPROVAL-REQUIREMENT-002 and APPROVAL-REQUIREMENT-003. An empty subject object does not identify a subject. A null eligibility declaration does not identify an eligibility rule. An applicability or state observation cannot replace these declarations at a concrete Decision boundary. Lightweight chain/composition observations remain governed by their own contracts; they need not repeat a concrete Requirement.

The bounded conformance representation is described in Conformance Conventions; it does not standardize every composing domain's subject or eligibility representation.

Rejection precedence in APPROVAL-REQUIREMENT-008 is a conservative control result over valid current evidence, not an evidence-conflict error. Opposing effective Decisions are individually valid and remain in history. Selecting the first or last Decision, choosing the latest timestamp, or letting approval win would make array order or undeclared lifecycle behavior financially decisive. A composing domain may define a distinct higher-level aggregation, but the standalone Requirement operation has one portable result for one effective set. This rule does not alter the quorum-specific opposing-vote validation in Approval Composition and creates no total priority among unrelated Approval validation errors.

The approval context in APPROVAL-REQUIREMENT-001 is the boundary within which a Requirement identifier is stable. A consumer that stores or transports Requirements in a larger namespace must retain which approval context and subject own the Requirement; equal Requirement identifiers in different contexts do not establish identity. This is an existing association obligation, not a requirement for a global registry or one prescribed identifier shape.

Example

The following JSON is illustrative and non-normative; eligibility is not limited to roles and these member names are not a portable serialization.

{
  "id": "finance-review",
  "eligibleRole": "FINANCE_REVIEWER",
  "state": "PENDING"
}

Invalid Examples

  • Treating permission to view an entity as approval of it.
  • Satisfying a requirement with a decision from an ineligible actor.

Open Questions

  • Should a future interchange specification define a portable representation for associating Approval Decisions with subject state or facts?
